fundamental_methodology_notes: Tier-1 official national-statistics adapters feed live macro state and override Tier-2 calendar state role-by-role; calendar data remains only a fallback for missing official roles.

Official adapters cover BLS/BEA, Eurostat, ONS, Japan official statistics, SECO/FSO, Statistics Canada, ABS and credential-free public Stats NZ information releases and fail closed independently when an endpoint changes.
Supplementary primary-source adapters broaden EUR inflation/labour, Japan CPI/labour/consumption, Swiss labour and New Zealand CPI/labour/GDP/retail coverage without weakening provenance rules.

The structural macro block is 30% of Phase 2. Inside that block, official policy carries 65% and Tier-3 World Bank annual background can contribute at most 35%, equivalent to 10.5% of Phase 2 before missing-data renormalization.
Fresh release state carries 15%; recent actual-versus-consensus and revision surprise carries 10%; CFTC positioning 25%; official central-bank communication 20%.

Official sovereign 2Y/10Y yield context is collected where practical and the 2Y-policy gap is exposed as a market-rate proxy, but is not separately weighted because it is not a pure policy-expectations measure.
Official commodity/export context is collected for commodity-sensitive AUD, CAD and NZD without adding a second directional weight that would double-count trade and macro evidence.
Tier-1 coverage raises live-state reliability; Tier-2 fallback provenance remains visible in every component.
Recent surprise evidence uses event-specific polarity, revision context and rapid time decay so old news does not masquerade as a current impulse.
Scheduled policy decisions, high-impact releases and official communication risk reduce confidence but do not change directional evidence.
